topics.title: Final Business Project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the components of a business plan.
The students should be able to explain the importance of market research in GSM repair business.
The students should be able to develop a simple business plan for a GSM repair shop.

Introduction:
We have learned about GSM repair tools and techniques. Today we will use this knowledge to create a business plan.

Content:
A business plan is a document that outlines your business goals and how to achieve them. For a GSM repair shop, include these sections: Executive Summary, Business Description, Market Analysis, Organization and Management, Service Line, Marketing and Sales, and Financial Projections. Market research helps you understand your customers and competitors. For example, check how much people in your area pay for screen repairs at Computer Village in Lagos.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to develop a business plan for a GSM repair shop in their local area.

Evaluation questions:
What are the main components of a business plan?
Why is market research important for a GSM repair business?
How would you price your services for a common phone repair like battery replacement?

Summary:
A well-written business plan is essential for starting and managing a successful GSM repair business.

topics.title: Exhibition and Product Display
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate proper repair techniques on common GSM faults.
The students should be able to display repair tools and equipment effectively.
The students should be able to explain the features of repaired GSM devices.

Introduction:
We have learned various repair skills. Today we will showcase these skills through demonstrations and displays.

Content:
For exhibition, organize your repair tools neatly on a table. Label each tool clearly. Prepare common phone faults like charging port issues, screen problems, and microphone failures. Demonstrate step-by-step how to fix them. Use local examples like Tecno or Infinix phones common in Nigerian markets. Create display boards showing before and after pictures of repairs. Practice explaining your work in simple English.

Class activity:
Students will set up exhibition booths displaying repair tools and demonstrating fixes on sample phones.

Evaluation questions:
Name three tools needed for GSM screen repair.
How would you explain to a customer why their phone won't charge?
What safety precautions should you take when repairing phones?

Summary:
Effective exhibition and demonstration of repair skills helps customers understand the value of your technical expertise.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship Fair Preparation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to prepare materials for BECE practical examination.
The students should be able to organize a presentation about GSM repair services.
The students should be able to handle common customer questions professionally.

Introduction:
We have learned business and repair skills. Now we will prepare to showcase these at our entrepreneurship fair.

Content:
For BECE practicals, gather all required tools and materials. Practice common repair tasks quickly and accurately. Create presentation posters showing your services and prices. Prepare answers to common customer questions like "How long will this take?" and "What is your warranty?" Role-play customer interactions. Practice using proper technical terms in simple language. For example, instead of "faulty charging port," say "port that won't connect charger."

Class activity:
Students will prepare their exhibition booths and practice customer service scenarios with feedback from the teacher.

Evaluation questions:
What materials should you prepare for BECE practical examination?
How would you explain a complex repair to a non-technical customer?
Why is professional communication important in GSM repair business?

Summary:
Proper preparation for entrepreneurship fair helps students demonstrate their skills and knowledge effectively.

topics.title: Mid-Term Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer questions on previous topics.
The students should be able to demonstrate practical skills learned.

Introduction:
Today we will write our mid-term examination to test what you have learned so far.
This examination covers all topics we have discussed this term.

Content:
The examination will include both theoretical and practical sections.
The theoretical part will test your knowledge of computer hardware components GSM repairs.
The practical part will require you to identify parts and perform basic troubleshooting.
Time allocated is 1 hour 30 minutes.

Class activity:
Students will write the examination in the examination hall.
They must bring their writing materials and follow all examination rules.

Evaluation questions:
1. List three types of computer RAM.
2. Explain what GSM stands for.
3. How do you fix a phone that won't charge?
4. Differentiate between hardware and software problems.

Summary:
The mid-term examination will assess your understanding of computer hardware and GSM repairs.

topics.title: Revision and BECE Preparation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall key concepts from JSS1-3.
The students should be able to identify common GSM faults and solutions.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper repair procedures.

Introduction:
We have covered many topics over three years. Today we will review important concepts and prepare for BECE.

Content:
Review fundamental concepts like GSM components, tools, and safety procedures. Practice identifying faults in phones brought from home. Common issues include charging problems, screen damage, and software glitches. Remember safety rules like disconnecting battery before repairs. Study past BECE questions and marking schemes. Practice using multimeters to test components. Review business aspects like pricing and customer service. Focus on practical skills needed for the examination.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to troubleshoot and repair sample phones with common faults.

Evaluation questions:
List three safety precautions when repairing GSM devices.
What steps would you follow to diagnose a phone that won't turn on?
How would you calculate the cost of replacing a phone screen?

Summary:
Thorough revision of all topics helps students perform well in BECE practical examination.

topics.title: BECE Examination and Closing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the components of a computer system, identify common hardware faults, explain the steps for troubleshooting GSM issues, and demonstrate proper handling of computer peripherals.

Introduction:
We have studied computer hardware and GSM repairs throughout the term. Now we will prepare for the BECE examination and review all topics covered.

Content:
The BECE examination covers computer hardware components like CPU, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and printer. Students should know how to identify common faults such as no power, display problems, or keyboard failure. For GSM repairs, focus on common issues like phone not charging, screen damage, and network problems. Always start with basic checks like power source and connections before opening any device.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to identify hardware components on a desktop computer and write down possible faults for each component.

Evaluation questions:
1. List three components of a computer system.
2. What is the first step to take when a GSM phone does not power on?
3. Explain how to check if a computer monitor is faulty.
4. Why is it important to handle computer peripherals carefully?

Summary:
Proper preparation for the BECE requires reviewing all hardware components and repair procedures covered in this term.
